title: The Art of Knowing What Matters
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: Better scores, but more learning?
scenes.viewerPurpose: Participation scores leave an important ability untested. Moves the evaluation of education and AI from circulating answers and activity scores toward usable understanding and judgment. Visible speed can miss meaningful effort.
scenes.composition: Show a classroom participation report improving while a new unaided problem remains unattempted. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.

Keep the students and their actual work beside the report instead of celebrating the score.

cues.text: The classroom's activity scores rise, but can students solve a new problem without the platform?
cues.visualAction: Show a classroom participation report improving while a new unaided problem remains unattempted.
cues.emotion: Concerned curiosity; gently emphasize “without the platform”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: The Art of Knowing What Matters argues that schools and AI should be judged by the abilities they help people develop.
cues.visualAction: Keep the students and their actual work beside the report instead of celebrating the score.
cues.emotion: Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “abilities they help people develop”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.

cues.text: A fast answer can hide uncertainty, while slower work may contain the learning a metric misses.
cues.visualAction: One student pauses over a method while another quickly submits an answer.
cues.emotion: Patient care; gently emphasize “slower work”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: An answer becomes a capacity
scenes.viewerPurpose: Information and judgment become understandable questions. The inquiry concerns human capabilities. Compression can leave important distinctions behind.
scenes.composition: Show the same information becoming a worked attempt at a new question. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Show the same information becoming a worked attempt at a new question.
Keep teacher, student and assisting tool visibly connected around one task.
A compact score leaves part of the student’s reasoning outside its frame.

cues.text: The book asks how information becomes something we can use, and how we decide what matters.
cues.visualAction: Show the same information becoming a worked attempt at a new question.
cues.emotion: Plain curiosity; gently emphasize “what matters”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: It follows education, institutions, and AI to examine which abilities our systems help people develop.
cues.visualAction: Keep teacher, student and assisting tool visibly connected around one task.
cues.emotion: Grounded interest; gently emphasize “help people develop”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: What gets lost when a complicated situation becomes a convenient summary or score?
cues.visualAction: A compact score leaves part of the student’s reasoning outside its frame.
cues.emotion: Quiet doubt; gently emphasize “summary or score”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: The judgment behind progress
scenes.viewerPurpose: The reader gains a concrete question to examine. The classroom opening leaves a meaningful uncertainty.
scenes.composition: A teacher returns to the student’s work before treating the report as progress. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.

cues.text: Teachers, builders, and curious readers can use these examples to question what counts as progress.
